root_cause.text: In __do_krealloc() and kvrealloc_node_align_noprof(), the reallocation fallback path either used uninitialized old size variables after an early jump (causing data loss) or copied the full old allocation size without bounding by the new size when shrinking (causing buffer overflow).
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the initialization of `ks` and `orig_size` before the `goto alloc_new` for the `__GFP_THISNODE` case, and bounds memcpy lengths with `min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks))` in __do_krealloc() and `min(size, ksize(p))` in kvrealloc_node_align_noprof(). The CVE description confirms both data loss and overflow bugs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect early reallocation for __GFP_THISNODE that forced new allocation even when size did not increase.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block that forced a new allocation when __GFP_THISNODE was set and the current memory node differed from the requested node, along with its associated comment.
intent_record.how: Before: if __GFP_THISNODE was set and the existing allocation was on a different node, krealloc would always allocate new memory even if the new size was smaller or equal. After: this special case is eliminated; krealloc only allocates new memory when the size actually requires it (e.g., larger size), preserving the current block otherwise.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix handling of __GFP_THISNODE in krealloc to force reallocation to the requested node when the current object is on a different node, regardless of size fit.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block that jumps to 'alloc_new' when __GFP_THISNODE flag is set and the current allocation is on a different node than requested, before the existing size-based reallocation check.
intent_record.how: When __GFP_THISNODE is specified and the current object resides on a different NUMA node, the function will attempt a new allocation on the target node even if the new size is smaller than the current allocation, overriding the default behavior of preserving the existing object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix krealloc to avoid copying more than new_size bytes when shrinking the allocation.
intent_record.what: Changed the size argument of memcpy from `orig_size ?: ks` to `min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks))`, wrapping the original size calculation with a minimum of new_size.
intent_record.how: Prevents copying more bytes than the new allocation can hold when the original object is larger than the requested new size, avoiding a buffer overflow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential buffer overflow in kvrealloc when shrinking allocation by limiting memcpy to the minimum of old and new sizes.
intent_record.what: Changed the third argument of memcpy from ksize(p) to min(size, ksize(p)).
intent_record.how: Prevents buffer overflow when reallocating to a smaller size by ensuring no more bytes are copied than the new allocation's size.

Fix a potential buffer overflow in kvrealloc when shrinking allocation by limiting memcpy to the minimum of old and new sizes.

relevance_review.reason: Group 0 focuses on fixing node reallocation semantics for __GFP_THISNODE, not on the uninitialized old size or unbounded copy size issues described in the vulnerability root cause.

The group directly addresses the buffer overflow vulnerability in kvrealloc (and krealloc) by bounding the memcpy to the minimum of old and new sizes when shrinking, which is exactly one of the issues described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This statement copies orig_size bytes (or ks if orig_size is zero) without bounding by the new allocation size. When shrinking, orig_size can be larger than the new size, causing a buffer overflow in the destination buffer.
This statement copies ksize(p) bytes, the full size of the old allocation, without bounding by the new allocation size. When shrinking, this overflows the destination buffer n.

vuln_statements.explanation: This memcpy uses orig_size (or ks if zero) as the copy length without bounding by the new allocation size. When shrinking, orig_size can be larger than the new size, causing a buffer overflow in the destination buffer.
This memcpy copies ksize(p) bytes, the full size of the old allocation, without bounding by the new allocation size. When shrinking, this overflows the destination buffer n.
